passDefinition: One distinct design, ownership, semantic-boundary or delivery question with an explicit reviewed decision. Repeated presets, process repetitions and timing samples are not additional passes or independent precision evidence.
rankingPolicy: The following ordering is a practical review priority, not an objective ranking of programmers or empirical proof that a style is universally best.

priorityOrder.decision: Add the maintained S2301 warning; retain Ruff FBT ownership.
Add native no-return-assign at warning with except-parens; preserve intentional grouped memoization.

priorityOrder.principle: Handle asynchronous results and settlement explicitly
priorityOrder.decision: Retain existing promise and typed void-return owners. Reject the noisy syntactic executor fallback after valid-state review.
Retain existing discriminated unions and exhaustive handling.
Retain existing public contract and injection rules.
Retain existing catch and exception owners.

priorityOrder.principle: Reduce nesting while preserving cohesive work
priorityOrder.decision: Retain semantic complexity and guard clauses; reject arbitrary size limits.

priorityOrder.principle: Test observable behavior with meaningful oracles
Keep comments useful and remove restatement
priorityOrder.decision: Retain existing comment owners; preserve rationale.

priorityOrder.principle: Remove duplicated knowledge without forcing abstractions
priorityOrder.decision: Use advisory evidence and manual design judgment.

validation.canonicalCommand: TMPDIR="$TASK_TMP" mise --no-config --no-env --no-hooks exec terraform@1.15.8 -- make verify
validation.canonicalResult: See the final combined-stack pull request description and its checks for the completed verification result.

decision: ship-warning; do not promote opinionated checks to error in this change
limitations: This is not a blanket ban on boolean data or every boolean-typed signature.
Ruff FBT permits keyword-only boolean flags, named calls and its documented compatibility and allowed-call exemptions.
S2301 covers a narrow typed subset of dispatch shapes. JSX files are excluded because upstream does not resolve named handlers passed to components.
S2301 misses multi-statement bodies, expression-bodied arrows and short-circuit dispatch; syntax-only projects remain outside its typed coverage.
Named options improve call-site readability without proving a single responsibility.
no-return-assign targets unparenthesized ambiguity. Parenthesized assignments and useful memoization remain valid; it does not establish general command/query separation.
The rejected executor fallback flags useful timer and microtask wrappers. Existing typed void-return coverage and its JSX exception remain authoritative.
Performance evidence distinguishes warm rule overhead from noisy fresh-process observations and does not claim full consumer-preset timing.
Warnings require manual review. API-changing rewrites and promotion to errors need separate evidence.

integration.evidence: Incoming Python discriminated-union fixes, declarative record parsing, bootstrap admission changes, runtime tests and Python 1.54.0 package pins are preserved. The measured TypeScript source snapshot is unchanged by those integrations. Bundle versions advance to 8.89.0 and 8.90.0 rather than reusing main version 8.88.0.

admission.gap: The shared JS/TS preset previously had no selector-parameter owner.
admission.harm: Callers cannot see the selected behavior without tracing a boolean and the callee.
admission.validBoundary: Preserve data, named options, upstream callback exemptions and JSX files after corpus review.
admission.smallestFix: Pin and enable the upstream rule as an advisory in typed non-JSX modules.

admission.defect: An accidental assignment in a returned expression changes state and returns the assigned value.
admission.owner: ESLint core; parameter-reassignment checks cover a different construct.
admission.gap: The shared preset did not check unparenthesized returned assignments.
admission.harm: A comparison can silently become a state change with a different result.
admission.validBoundary: Preserve explicitly parenthesized assignments and intentional lazy memoization.
admission.smallestFix: Enable the upstream except-parens option as an advisory without intent-changing autofix.

admission.defect: A returned executor value does not settle a native Promise.

corpus.selection: Tracked, existing TypeScript/TSX source in the declared include subsets; this is not a claim of whole-repository or fleet coverage.

final.sampling: All 18 preliminary candidate findings were inspected. Final candidate findings are zero, so precision is not estimated from live positives. Seeded integration vectors establish positive coverage.
final.directiveAccounting: The selected-rule runner cannot resolve every unrelated consumer inline rule directive. Those 46 nonfatal diagnostics were excluded from candidate counts; they are not candidate findings or parser failures.

Both were working timer/microtask wrappers. Default activation was rejected.

performance.scope: The fixed 160-file public TypeScript source snapshot; baseline is the native Sarj plugin strict preset. This does not measure the full shared consumer preset or private projects.
performance.warmProtocol: One isolated process for one bounded corpus batch. Warm both variants, then run four pairs with alternating order. Each call discards diagnostic objects after aggregate counts; all variants see identical files.
performance.interpretation: No slowdown was observed in the paired warm median. Large VM-load and cache variation in fresh-process and individual paired timings prevents a speedup claim or a precise end-to-end overhead estimate. Keep warning severity; measure representative consumer latency during the warning release. Warm peak RSS includes both ESLint instances and shared parser caches, so it is not an incremental rule-memory estimate.

implementation.verificationBuildReuse: Make docs-artifacts-check already builds TypeScript. Its third-party catalog check now passes --typescript-built and continues to project/check all artifacts; standalone generation still builds by default. Internal APIs use named required/prepared modes.
